Subject: Post-call recap: model fit & quantization tradeoffs (FinWave)

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on model fit, evals, and the quantization trade study we discussed.

Key takeaways from today's discovery:
- Primary workload: document summarization + policy extraction for compliance reviews (average input ~1.2k tokens; peak 8k).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 700ms for single-request, synchronous calls.
- Cost sensitivity: prioritizing >2x token-cost reduction vs FP16 baseline without >5% drop in QA accuracy on our prompt set.
- Security: data stays in your VPC (Private deployment); procurement will want SOC2 artifacts — already prepping.

Recommended models to evaluate (initial shortlist):
1) Llama-2-70B-chat (FP16) — baseline for highest quality, higher cost.
2) Falcon-40B-instruct — strong instruction-following; good throughput when quantized.
3) Mistral-7B / Mistral-7B-v0 variants — lower-cost, competitive on many instruction tasks; great for caching-heavy workloads.

Quantization/throughput approaches to consider:
- AWQ (4-bit): best throughput gains on many GPUs; generally small quality delta on instruction tasks but workload-dependent.
- GPTQ (4-bit): often higher fidelity for some generative tasks; toolchain maturity varies by model.
- FP8 / mixed FP8 (experimental): middle ground — better numeric fidelity than 4-bit ints, fewer mature kernels currently available.

Action items / next steps:
- Marissa/Dev: share the prompt set and the trade-study PDF + Drive folder with your team (attached).
- FinWave: confirm the representative test dataset (we discussed a 200-case eval slice).
- Schedule: demo + side-by-side eval run next Tue (2026-09-22) — suggest a 30-min slot to review results.

Attachments: finwave-quantization-trade-study-20260920.pdf, finwave-prompt-set-v1.json

Thanks — looking forward to the eval run.

—
Marissa Cole

Samir — quick technical notes to clarify the tradeoffs and what we'll run in the side-by-side: 

- Quantization impact (summary):
  * AWQ (4-bit, integer-backed): typically 3-4x token throughput vs FP16 on A100/H100 for decoder-only models. Quality delta often <3% absolute on instruction-following benchmarks, but edge cases (numeric extraction, entity-level precision) can show larger regressions.
  * GPTQ (4-bit): often preserves more of the model distribution for certain weight matrices; can outperform AWQ on some generative/fluency metrics but is model-dependent.
  * FP8 / mixed FP8: offers a middle path — better fidelity than 4-bit integer quant, lower memory than FP16; kernel support still evolving (best on newer runtimes/hardware).

- Fallbacks/routing: Redwood can set per-route policies: e.g., try AWQ-quantized variant first, if quality checks fail for a request or a batch (we instrument server-side eval hooks), route to FP16 or a higher-precision variant. We can demo automatic fallback during the eval run.

- Latency expectations (high level, p95):
  * FP16 (Llama-2-70B) on H100: ~600-900ms for 1.2k avg input depending on batch and KV caching.
  * AWQ 4-bit (Falcon-40B) on H100: p95 often drops to ~200-350ms for same workload.
  * FP8 builds show ~1.5-2x improvement vs FP16 in our prototype tests. Exact numbers will depend on sequence length and batching.

- Eval harness: we'll run side-by-side on your 200-case slice with the following metrics measured: exact-match for extractions, ROUGE-L for summaries, token-per-second, cost-per-1M tokens, and qualitative failure tagging. Results will be posted to the Drive folder and a short trade-study PDF (attached).

I've attached the trade-study PDF with per-model numbers (A100/H100 ops) and the prompt set JSON. If you want, we can also run an additional GPTQ variant on Falcon-40B — takes ~2x the compile/tuning time vs AWQ but worth it if extraction precision matters.

Attachments: finwave-quantization-trade-study-20260920.pdf, finwave-prompt-set-v1.json
